en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Holy Immeasurable Life Resolute Radiance King, Spoken by the Buddha,
translated in Central India at Nālandā in Magadha, Western Heaven (India).
Translated by the Imperial Subject, the Dharma Master of Rantasi, the Tripitaka Master, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Fātian, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the World-Honored One...
At Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
he was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus;
all of them had exhausted their outflows, attained liberation of mind, and were free from further afflictions.
Having attained his own benefit, his mind was well-liberated;
he was a great Arhat known to all,
and possessed further wisdom and vast merit.
The honored ones, adorned with majestic deportment and fully endowed with all virtues,
as well as the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others,
have all assembled here for the sake of hearing the Dharma.
In that assembly, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, Great in Wisdom, was the foremost. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha,
out of compassion for all short-lived sentient beings in future ages, [spoke thus].
To cause their lifespan to increase and to obtain great benefit,
he preached for them the inconceivable, secret, profound, subtle, and supreme Dharma.
At that time...
The World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and said:
"Listen attentively, you all!
From here, in this Jambudvīpa..."
To the west, beyond immeasurable Buddha-fields,
there is a world named Immeasurable Treasury of Merits.
The land is magnificent and adorned with various precious jewels.
Pure, sublime, peaceful, and blissful,
surpassing all that is subtle and foremost throughout the ten directions—
within that world-system, the Treasury of Immeasurable Merits.
There is a Buddha named Amitāyus-niyata-prabhā-rāja Tathāgata, Unsurpassed Perfectly Enlightened One,
who currently resides in that world,
giving rise to great compassion to expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.
May they obtain supreme benefit, peace, and happiness.
The Buddha again addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"In this world-system of Jambudvīpa, the lifespan of humans is now one hundred years."
Among them, many who have committed various evil deeds meet with untimely death.

However, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, if there are sentient beings who obtain and behold this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Decisive Radiance*, [they shall not suffer such fates].
Regarding the excellence of these merits and the hearing of this name:
whether one writes it oneself or instructs another to write out this sutra in its entirety,
whether in one's own residence or on a high tower.
Or, one may install it within the halls and chapels of a vihāra,
upholding, reciting, honoring, and prostrating before it with various exquisite flowers, burnt incense, and powdered incense.
With incense, flower garlands, and other offerings,
one should make offerings to the *Tathāgata King of the Determinate Radiance of Immeasurable Life Dhāraṇī Sūtra*.
For such people of short lifespan, [this shall be their refuge].
If one can, with a sincere heart, copy, receive and uphold,
recite, offer worship to, and prostrate before [this],
such a person shall further increase their lifespan to a full hundred years.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,
if there are sentient beings who hear the name of this Tathāgata Infinite Life Resolute Radiance King,
and if they can sincerely recite it one hundred and eight times;
Thus, these short-lived sentient beings shall have their lifespans increased;
or even those who merely hear his name and,
with a sincere heart, accept it with faith and veneration.
Such a person shall also gain an increase in their lifespan.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, if there is one who at all times never abandons this in mind for even a moment, [they shall likewise attain these benefits].
With sincere resolve, you should seek the sublime Dharma.
Good sons and good daughters, you should listen attentively.
I shall now recite for you the *Dhāraṇī of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Resolute Radiance*, which says:
Namo bhagavate āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tathāgatāya arhate.

Ghaṭe svāhā | Pāpaviśodhani mahānaya-parivāre svāhā | Oṃ Mañjuśrī-kumārabhūta.
If there is anyone who personally transcribes this *Dhāraṇī of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Tathāgata King of the Decisive Radiance of Immeasurable Life*,
or instructs another to transcribe this *dhāraṇī*.
Place it atop a high tower or within a pure location inside a hall,
and provide various offerings, adorned according to the Dharma.
Those of short lifespan shall further obtain long life, fulfilling a hundred years.
Such persons, when their lives end hereafter in this place,
will immediately attain rebirth in the world-system called the Treasury of Immeasurable Merit within the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata King of Determinate Radiance of Immeasurable Life.
When Śākyamuni Buddha was preaching this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life King of Determinate Radiance*,
there were ninety-nine koṭis of buddhas present.
With single-minded devotion, they spoke with different mouths but in one voice,
reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life and Resolute Radiance*.
At that time, there were furthermore eighty-four koṭis of buddhas.
With single-mindedness, they spoke with different mouths but in one voice,
reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life and Resolute Radiance*.
At that time, there were also seventy-seven koṭis of Buddhas.
With single-minded devotion, they spoke with different mouths but in one voice,
reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Resolute Radiance*.
At that time, there were also sixty-six koṭis of Buddhas.
With single-mindedness, they spoke with different mouths but in one voice,
also reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Resolute Radiance*.
At that time, there were also fifty-five koṭis of Buddhas.
With single-mindedness, they spoke with different mouths but in one voice,
reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Decisive Radiance*.
At that time, there were also forty-four koṭis of Buddhas.
With single-minded focus, they spoke with one voice in unison,
reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Resolute Radiance*.
At that time, there were also thirty-six koṭis of Buddhas.
With single-mindedness, they spoke with different mouths but in one voice,
likewise reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Resolute Radiance*.
At that time, there were also twenty-five koṭis of Buddhas.
With single-mindedness, they spoke with different mouths but in one voice,
also reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Decisive Radiance*.
At that time, there were also Buddhas numbering as many as the sands of ten *gaṅgā* rivers and *koṭi*s.
Each with no difference in mind, they spoke with one voice,
all reciting this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Resolute Radiance*.
Regarding this dhāraṇī sūtra,
if there is anyone who either writes it themselves or instructs others to write it,
such a person, in the future...
They shall not fall into hell, nor into the realm of hungry ghosts, nor into the animal realm;
they shall not fall into the world of King Yama, the dark official of the path of karma.
They shall never again undergo the retribution of evil within these various miserable realms.
By the power of the merit from thus transcribing this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of the Decisive Radiance of Immeasurable Life*,
such a person, in all future births, will...
In life after life, one shall attain the knowledge of past existences.
If one writes this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Resolute Radiance* oneself,
or teaches others to write it, [one shall obtain these benefits].
Such a person is identical to one who has transcribed the eighty-four thousand treasuries of the Dharma;
the merit obtained shall be no different.
This is the *Tathāgata Aparimitāyur-jñāna-nirdeśa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
If there is another person who either writes it themselves or instructs others to write it,
such a person is equivalent to one who has constructed eighty-four thousand precious stupas;
the merit obtained is no different.
Regarding this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Decisive Radiance*:
if one writes it oneself or instructs another to write it,
such a person— even if they possess karma for the five deeds of immediate retribution— [shall be purified].
By the power of these merits,
all such karmic deeds will be completely eliminated through this *Tathāgata Aparimitāyur-jñāna-niyata-prabhāsa-rāja-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
Whether one writes it oneself or instructs others to write it,
such a person shall not fall into the realm of the Māra king or his retinue,
nor shall they fall into the paths of yakṣas or rākṣasas.
One shall not fall into untimely or unnatural death,
nor shall one ever again undergo these various evil retributions.
This is the *Sūtra of the Dharani of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Decisive Radiance*.
Whether one writes it oneself or instructs another to write it,
when such a person approaches the end of life,
there will be ninety-nine koṭis of Buddhas.
He will manifest his face before them to welcome them,
and they shall be reborn in that Buddha-land.
You all should not give rise to doubt or uncertainty.
Regarding this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Decisive Radiance*:
if one writes it oneself or instructs another to write it,
such a person shall never again receive a female body in the future.
If one writes this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of Immeasurable Life’s Decisive Radiance* oneself,
or instructs another to write it,
such a person will always receive the protection of the Eastern Vidyādhara, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
In the south is Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the World-Protecting King who is the Lord of the Kumbhāṇḍas;
in the west is Virūpākṣa, the World-Protecting King who is the Lord of the Great Nāgas;
and in the north is Vaiśravaṇa, the World-Protecting King who is the Lord of the Great Yakṣas.
They shall secretly conceal their forms to follow and protect them.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who, for the sake of this sutra,
is able to give even a small portion of wealth or treasures as an offering;
Suppose this person were to take all seven treasures—
gold, silver, lapis lazuli, mother-of-pearl, agate, coral, and amber—
filling the entirety of a trichiliocosm, and offer them all as a gift in alms.
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who makes offerings to this sutra,
they are thereby making offerings to the entire treasury of the true Dharma.
Moreover, if there should be anyone who can take the most exquisite of the seven precious jewels...
I made offerings to Vipaśyin;
I tested [the practice] under Śikhin.
K Krakucchanda, K Kanakamuni, and K Kāśyapa.
The merit obtained by the Tathāgata, Arhat,
Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni cannot be measured or its quantity known; yet,
if there should be anyone who makes offerings to this *Tathāgatāparimitāyurjñānanirdeśa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, the King of Infinite Life and Resolute Radiance, [their merit shall be even greater].
The merit thus obtained likewise cannot be measured or its limits known.
It is like the waters of the four great oceans filling them to the brim;
one could not know the number of even a single drop.
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who copies, makes offerings to, upholds,
and recites this *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Tathāgata King of the Determinate Radiance of Immeasurable Life*,
the merit they obtain will likewise be immeasurable, such that its limit cannot be calculated or known.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who transcribes this *Sūtra of the Dharani of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life’s Decisive Radiance*,
the site and ground where it is kept shall become a precious stupa containing the true-body relics of all Buddhas.
One should respect and prostrate to it.
If there are sentient beings who hear this dhāraṇī with their ears,
these beings shall never again receive the bodies of flying birds, quadrupeds, or other species with many feet.
In the future, they will swiftly attain the realization of non-retrogressive, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Furthermore,
if there is a person who accumulates gold, silver, lapis lazuli, mother-of-pearl, agate, coral, and amber;
If one were to give away all seven precious jewels, as vast as the King of Mountains, Meru,
the resulting merit would be immeasurable and its quantity impossible to know. Yet,
if there should be someone who [recites] this *Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Tathāgata King of Infinite Life, Resolute Radiance*,...
Furthermore, the merit obtained by one who is able to practice such giving cannot be measured or its limit known. Moreover,
if there is another person who transcribes this *Sūtra of the Immeasurable Life Resolute Radiance King Tathāgata Dhāraṇī*, [the merit they obtain is likewise immeasurable].
As for those who pay homage and make offerings,
such persons are paying homage and making offerings to all Tathāgatas in all Buddha-fields of the ten directions,
without any difference.
At that time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni spoke these verses:
"By practicing the power of giving, one achieves accomplishment; Through the power of giving, one attains Buddhahood."
If one enters the chamber of great compassion and hears this dhāraṇī even for a moment,
though their practice of giving may not yet be perfected, such a person will swiftly realize the state of a Teacher of Gods and Humans;
through the power of cultivating and maintaining the precepts, they shall attain Buddhahood by virtue of that power of upholding the precepts.
If one enters the chamber of great compassion and briefly hears this dhāraṇī,
even if their observance of the precepts is not yet complete, such a person will swiftly realize the state of a Teacher of Gods and Humans;
by accomplishing the power of practicing patience, and through the power of patience, they shall attain Buddhahood.
If one enters the chamber of great compassion and briefly hears this dhāraṇī,
even if their power of patience is not yet perfected, such a person will swiftly realize the state of a Teacher of Gods and Humans;
through the accomplishment of the power of diligent practice, and by virtue of that power of diligence, they shall attain Buddhahood.
If one enters the chamber of great compassion and hears this dhāraṇī even for a moment,
though their diligent practice may not yet be perfected, such a person will swiftly realize the state of a Teacher of Gods and Humans;
through the accomplishment of the power of meditative concentration, they shall attain Buddhahood by virtue of that power of concentration.
If one enters the chamber of great compassion and briefly hears this dhāraṇī,
even if their meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) is not yet perfected, such a person will swiftly realize the state of a Teacher of Gods and Humans.
By accomplishing the power of wisdom through practice, and by virtue of that power of wisdom, they shall attain Buddhahood.
If one enters the chamber of great compassion and hears this dhāraṇī even for a moment,
though their wisdom may not yet be perfected, such a person will swiftly realize the state of a Teacher of Gods and Humans.
Having spoken this sutra, the Buddha—
The great assembly of bhikṣus, as well as the bodhisattvas,
and all the world— including devas, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Holy King of Immeasurable Life Spoken by the Buddha.
